subject: DMRs for more than two groups (control and treatment and beyond)

messages.author: cbaf432548852c3b
messages.subject: DMRs for more than two groups (control and treatment and beyond)
parts:
Dear Dr Altuna, 

Good day to you. I would like to seek your advise. 

I have a project with 4 groups: 
Control, 
Induced disease, 
drugA-induced disease,
drugB-induced disease 

each group with 3 biological replicates. 

Any way in methylKit to support these kind of analysis simultaneously? or I should have to compare three other groups to control, respectively?

Thanks for your kind reply and help. 

Best wishes, 
Wai Feng

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMRs for more than two groups (control and treatment and beyond)
parts:
Dear Wai,
It supports these kind of analysis but when you put all the groups at once, you will get regions where there is a difference between groups but you will not exactly know which pairs have the difference. For that you need to do pairwise comparison with methylKit.

Best
Altuna

Thanks Dr Altuna.

I have three more questions hopefully can get your valuable opinion, Dr.

In the methylKit user guide, it suggests one can approach pool() function in the presence of replicates, so in my case biological replicates.

Q1-Could you please help me go through if my commands sequence are correct?

> file.list=list(system.file("extdata", "a_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "b_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "c_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "d_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "e_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "f_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "g_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "h_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"))

> myobj=methRead(file.list,sample.id=list("a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h"),assembly="rn6",treatment=c(1,1,1,1,0,0,0,0))

> filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL, hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

> norm.myobj <- normalizeCoverage(filtered.myobj, method="median")

> meth <- unite(norm.myobj, destrand=TRUE, min.per.group = 3L)

> meth

> pooled.meth <- pool(meth, sample.ids = c("test","control"))

> myDiff <- calculateDiffMeth(pooled.meth, num.cores = 4)

... ...



Q2-Or I should add the tiling window analysis (i have done that before > pooled.meth <- pool(meth, sample.ids = c("test","control")) command as show above? I have tried that but seems dont have any effect, results are the same.

Q3Also, if my replicates (n) for each group is: Control (n=3), induced disease (n=3), drugA-induced disease (n=3),  drugA-induced disease (n=2), 'm I using the command correctly as shown below?

> file.list=list(system.file("extdata", "a_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "b_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "c_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "d_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "e_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "f_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "g_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"))

> myobj=methRead(file.list,sample.id=list("a","b","c","d","e","f","g"),assembly="rn6",treatment=c(1,1,1,1,0,0,0))


many thanks for your time, Dr Altuna

On Thu, Feb 8, 2018 at 1:29 AM, <limwai...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks Dr Altuna.

I have three more questions hopefully can get your valuable opinion, Dr.

In the methylKit user guide, it suggests one can approach pool() function in the presence of replicates, so in my case biological replicates.

Q1-Could you please help me go through if my commands sequence are correct?

> file.list=list(system.file("extdata", "a_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "b_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "c_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "d_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "e_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "f_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "g_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "h_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"))
Why are you doing this ? system.file() is for reaching the files that come with the package. just pass the paths to files

> myobj=methRead(file.list,sample.id=list("a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h"),assembly="rn6",treatment=c(1,1,1,1,0,0,0,0))

> filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL, hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9) 

> norm.myobj <- normalizeCoverage(filtered.myobj, method="median")

> meth <- unite(norm.myobj, destrand=TRUE, min.per.group = 3L)

> meth

> pooled.meth <- pool(meth, sample.ids = c("test","control"))

> myDiff <- calculateDiffMeth(pooled.meth, num.cores = 4)

... ...
Looks OK, but why are you pooling, you have many replicates.

Q2-Or I should add the tiling window analysis (i have done that before > pooled.meth <- pool(meth, sample.ids = c("test","control")) command as show above? I have tried that but seems dont have any effect, results are the same.
don't understand the question. results are the same compared with what? if you are tiling the results should not be the same, you will have different coordinates for tiles not individual CpGs.

Q3Also, if my replicates (n) for each group is: Control (n=3), induced disease (n=3), drugA-induced disease (n=3),  drugA-induced disease (n=2), 'm I using the command correctly as shown below?

> file.list=list(system.file("extdata", "a_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "b_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "c_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "d_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "e_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "f_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "g_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"))

> myobj=methRead(file.list,sample.id=list("a","b","c","d","e","f","g"),assembly="rn6",treatment=c(1,1,1,1,0,0,0))

Please check and correct your question if needed. You have control, induced diseased, 2 times drugA-induced disease. If you sum up the "n" it makes 11, but you have only 7 samples. the question and your code doesn't match.

many thanks for your time, Dr Altuna

Dear Dr Altuna, 

Good day to you. Appreciate for your reply and sorry for some confusing questions here. 

Q1 - Alright, Dr. I will do so. 

Q2 - I will try to analyze again with our new data. 

Q3 - Sorry, Dr. One of them should be drugB-induced disease (n=2), for this model, we can only have n=2 but not n=3 as it is the offspring from previous generation, we could not get anymore. 

* I have corrected my question here. Kindly, please help me check if I'm using the command correctly. 

I have four groups as listed below 
Control (n=3), a_CpG.txt, b_CpG.txt, c_CpG.txt
induced disease (n=3), d_CpG.txt, e_CpG.txt, f_CpG.txt
drugA-induced disease (n=3),  g_CpG.txt, h_CpG.txt, i_CpG.txt
drugB-induced disease (n=2), j_CpG.txt, k_CpG.txt

1. To compare between control and induced disease, 

> file.list=list(system.file("extdata", "d_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "e_C02-4_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "f_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "a_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "b_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "c_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"))
> myobj=methRead(file.list,sample.id=list("d", "e", "f", "a", "b", "c"),assembly="rn6",treatment=c(1,1,1,0,0,0))

> meth=unite(myobj, destrand=FALSE)
> meth.min=unite(myobj.min.per.group=3L)

*** is it correct?

2. To compare control and drugA-induced disease,
I use the similar command stated in 1, by replacing to g_CpG.txt, h_CpG.txt, i_CpG.txt 

3. To compare control and drugB-induced disease, 
>  file.list=list(system.file("extdata", "j_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "k_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "a_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "b_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "c_CpG.txt", package = "methylKit")) 
> myobj=methRead(file.list.sample.id=list("j","k","a","b","c"),assembly='rn6',treatment=c(1,1,0,0,0))
> meth=unite(myobj, destrand=FALSE)
> meth.min=unite(myobj.min.per.group=3L)

*** For meth.min=unite(myobj.min.per.group, should I just put 2L, since the lowest sample in drugB just n=2? If yes, should I apply 2L to all of my analysis throughout this project? So that all parameters are the same and comparable.  

4. For methylKit, can I compare all four groups that I have in the same time? Or I should only analyze two groups, which are "control" and "test" in each time as described above? 

Appreciate for your reply and your help, Dr. 

Thank you so much! 


Thank you very much and have a nice day!

Best wishes, 
Wai Feng
